evidence: Reads as: "go ahead and notice who’s doing the noticing (more on that in Noticing Counts, further on), or borrow an adult...". "That" has a clear referent in the same sentence (the noticing-who-is-noticing instruction), and "Noticing Counts" is a real heading (### Noticing Counts, line 205 of the guide, versus this section at line 131), whose text does expand on whoever's noticing not being all the way inside the scared one. So "further on" is accurate and the old forward-pointing "as described in" is fixed. "Further on" is the author's own pointer idiom elsewhere in the guide. It adds no claim, tone or first person. The parenthetical sits naturally in a casual, jokey sentence and does not interrupt the borrowed-adult clause. No tell row applies: C02 absent (referent found), T26 none ("noticing" repeated only because it is the heading's name), T11/T19 not a bridge or announcement but a short pointer.
